data.narrative:
Canada Rocket Company is a seed-stage space and aerospace developer founded by Hugh Kolias and David Tenny, having raised $6.2M to date. The valuation universe spans five public comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) with a median P/S of 24.4x, and eight private-stage peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and ICEYE, though narrow-filter peer matching within the seed/adjacent-stage cohort yielded insufficient datapoints for robust median-comp anchoring.

Of three valuation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. Using the $6.2M raised as a value proxy and applying a typical seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.5x yields an implied valuation of $16M. Peer-median anchoring failed due to sparse comparable data within the same stage and valuation tier (fewer than three matches). Public-comp P/S anchoring could not be applied without disclosed revenue figures, standard for private companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $13M to $18M, centered on $16M. This range is grounded in a single method and carries material uncertainty around the assumed step-up multiplier and the absence of narrowly comparable private peers at seed stage. A revenue-generating milestone or closed funding round would enable public-comp and peer-median triangulation, materially strengthening conviction in any revised valuation.
